institutionName: Panteion University of Social and Political Sciences

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A destination quite far from Denmark in terms of climate and culture, and that it was a big city with many cultural opportunities while being close to nature. It was also important for me that it was a affordable destination. 
 Athens is great because you can easily take a ferry to the islands or rent a car to go to the mountains, while still being a big city with many opportunities. And the food is amazing!! and cheap!!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Athens is very vibrant and many events are taking place! from film festivals to concerts and political events

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was quite easy finding accomondation in Athens, the university forwarded me some websites they recommended for renting. 
On the other hand was it hard to find information about the courses available at Panteion. My advice is to not spend to much time on searching for courses beforehand, everything will be way easier when you are there:)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved assisteance from the ersamus office and from the people involved in the ESN (erasmus student netwotk). In genral if you need assistence, the erasmus coordinator at Panteion is responding quit fast by email or you can always visit the office at university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy! I found a room through StayInAthens. It worked easy but the appartment was not that nice. Many of my friends found appartments through facebook or through anither site I dont remember the name of... But overall it should be fine to find a place

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I lived in Exarchia and I would really recommend living there. It is the anarcistic and left oriented area with many bars, cafes and restaurants. BUT it is becomming really gentrified and it is imporatnt to know that you are contributuing to that process, if you choose to find a place to stay there. Often we ended up hanging out in that area, and then it was really nice to be able to just walk home. 
Besides Exarchia is the areas Kipsili, pangrati and koukaki also really nice. Victoria is also good and affordable, but many locals would never recommend that area because it is the immigrant area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is really important that you dont spend too much time upon arrival on finding out how to register to courses. You will get the info when being there and the deadline for choosing the final courses is alomst two months after semester start. So dobnt stress about it, everything works out in the end:)) 
But it is really a different process then what you are used to at KU

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you get a schedule of the courses the week you start at the university. Then you can try out different courses and after almost two month you officially register for the courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the erasmus office was always open for assistence

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: again dont stress about it, and maybe try to choose some courses that dont have to big essays to write in the end. I ended up only having courses where I had to write essays for my exams, and I therefore spended a lot of time in the library. And some courses without any form of eaxams and that was nice because I had so many assignments to write.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the experience that panteion dosen't prioritize Erasmus courses that high. None of my courses really went in depth with their topics and felt quite superficial. I almost didint have any lectures og seminars in several of my courses and I ended up spending more time in the library than at classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is not that high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I bit similar just with way less resources.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Critical Theories and Ethnographies of Precarity, Precariousness and Care
Anthropology of Dance 
Key issues in Psychology – Erasmus
Environment, Infrastructures, Development: Anhropological Perspectives
Managing diversity in different life domains

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the course, Environment, Infrastructures, Development: Anhropological Perspectives, I think it was the only course where I had a big outpout from. The professor is interesting and you read interesting texts.
Also, Managing diversity in different life domains, beacuse the professor is so funny in a weird way and you just have to attend the coruse to pass.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I just spended a lot of money on travelling, but that is well spended money! also etaling and drinking a lot out! even though it is cheap, it becomes expensive if ypu do it every day....

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the prizes in the supermarkets are quite similar to Denmark which really surprised me. Always buy your vegetables at the local market

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university has so many sport opportunities and they are all for free! I played tennis twice a week and also too som pilates classes

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all kinds of sports

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
there are plenty of cultural events taking place in athens. You can look at
kinomatorama.net
for activities, it is a left oriented websites that has a calender for events taking place in Athens. Especially political events

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to the islands! but also the mainland is so so beautifull! especially peleponies and the mountains in the north

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. But athens is way more chaotic than copenhagen. I like that but can also be exhausting

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I almost only had erasmus friends... but i took classes at a local dancing studio and there i found some friends. So engage yourself with some kind of sport outside of university or do som volunteer work in som of the citys many squatted places

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Greeks are very social and o out a lot!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: enjoy living in a city with a warmer climate and where it is way more affordable to go out than in copenhagen. And admire how political the greek youth is!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't expect to much from the study program.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be inspired from the people you meet and the place you are staying

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I dont know:))

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
